h1: Bloom Cafe & Hostel — A Spotless Hostel on Walking Street With a Great Coffee Cafe Downstairs
intro: Koh Lipe is known for pricey beachfront stays, but if you're travelling as a backpacker or want to save your budget for diving, Bloom Cafe & Hostel is the name that comes up most often · a 2-star hostel in the middle of Walking Street (the island's central lane) that earns special praise for cleanliness · dorm beds have privacy curtains, stairs instead of ladders up to the bunks, lockers and strong AC, and there's a specialty-coffee cafe with breakfast downstairs · rates start at around ฿320/bed for a dorm, making it a go-to base when you want a clean, central place to sleep without paying beachfront-resort prices.
galleryAlts: Bunk beds in a Bloom Hostel dorm room with privacy curtains and stairs up to the bunk
The downstairs cafe at Bloom Cafe & Hostel with a relaxed feel, serving coffee and breakfast
A clean Bloom Hostel room with strong AC and freshly made beds

body.html: The first thing nearly every review mentions is cleanliness · Bloom is a hostel where someone is cleaning the bathrooms and common areas almost constantly · sheets and towels are changed daily and beds are made every morning — a standard you rarely find at this price · on an island like Koh Lipe where fresh water and electricity are limited, having genuinely clean bathrooms and AC that actually gets cold is the reason guests cite most for coming back.

There are several room types · on the dorm side there's an 8-bed mixed dorm, a 4-bed female-only dorm and a 6-bed dorm with shared bathroom · what sets Bloom apart from the usual dorm is that the bunk beds use stairs rather than ladders, and every bed has a privacy curtain, a power outlet and a locker · if you'd rather not share, there's a Private Double Room with a shared bathroom that reviews describe as having comfy beds and a shared bathroom that isn't shared with many people · opened in 2017 and renovated in 2022, the rooms look newer than comparable hostels on the island.
"The cleanest hostel I've stayed at on the island — the bed curtains close all the way so it sleeps like a private room, and step out the door and you're surrounded by restaurants and dive shops."

Another standout is the downstairs cafe, which takes its specialty coffee seriously · several reviews say the coffee here is a notch above the usual island cafes · the morning menu has smoothie bowls, fruit bowls and breakfasts that guests praise for fresh ingredients · note that breakfast isn't included in the room rate — you order it at the cafe — though free coffee and tea are available in the common area · the cafe has a relaxed feel and makes a good spot to work, plan tours or meet fellow travellers.

Location is Bloom's trump card · it sits right in the middle of Walking Street, so you step out the door into restaurants, mini-marts, dive shops and tour desks all within walking distance · it's about a 5-minute walk to Pattaya Beach, with Sunrise and Sunset beaches a 10–15 minute walk away · the hostel has a desk to help book boat tours and ferry tickets, plus lockers, a first-aid room, and staff that reviews call friendly and helpful.

To be straight with you, the trade-off for a central Walking Street location is noise · Bloom is next to Maya Bar, so on nights the bar runs late you may hear music, especially in the front rooms · it's also not on the beach, so if you want to open your door onto the sea this isn't it · and because it's popular, beds book up fast — reserve ahead in high season · but in hostel terms, these gripes are minor next to what you get.

The takeaway from real guest reviews: Bloom Cafe & Hostel is ideal for solo travellers, budget-minded couples or backpackers who want a clean, central place to sleep and save their money for diving · cleanliness, curtained dorm beds and a good coffee cafe are what push it to the top of Koh Lipe's hostels · if you want a sea view at your door or total silence to fully unwind, look at a beachfront stay instead — but for value at a central hostel, this one genuinely delivers.

honestSummary: Bloom Cafe & Hostel Koh Lipe is a hostel that delivers cleanliness and a central island location at a budget price — ideal for solo travellers, budget-minded couples or backpackers who want to sleep well and save their money for diving · curtained dorm beds, a good coffee cafe and helpful staff are the highlights · but accept that it's next to a bar so there's some noise, it isn't on the beach, and dorms are shared-sleeping.
honestChecks: If you want to open your door onto the sea — Bloom is in the middle of Walking Street, not on the beach, about a 5-minute walk to the sand → choose a beachfront resort on Sunrise or Pattaya Beach instead.
If you're a light sleeper — the hostel is next to Maya Bar and on the central lane, so late bar nights can be audible → ask for an inner room or pack earplugs.
If you need full privacy — dorms are shared sleeping, even with bed curtains → book the Private Double Room or look at a private-room stay on the island instead.

tips.title: Ask for an inner room to dodge bar noise
tips.body: The hostel is next to Maya Bar and on the central lane. When booking, request a bed or room set back from the street, and pack earplugs for an easier night.

tips.title: Try the coffee and smoothie bowls at the cafe
tips.body: The downstairs cafe does specialty coffee that reviews single out. Breakfast isn't included but it's worth ordering, especially the fruit bowls.

tips.title: Book ahead — beds fill fast in high season
tips.body: Bloom is a popular hostel; dorm beds and the Private room fill quickly Nov–Apr. Book ahead and lock a free-cancellation rate first.

tips.title: Let the desk handle boats and tours
tips.body: The hostel has a desk to book boat tours and ferry tickets. Tell them your arrival and departure boats in advance for the smoothest trip.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Bloom Cafe & Hostel Koh Lipe

faq.q: Where is Bloom Cafe & Hostel on Koh Lipe and how do you get there?
faq.a: It sits in the middle of Walking Street, the island's central lane, on Koh Lipe, Satun Province · about a 5-minute walk to Pattaya Beach and 12–15 minutes to Sunrise/Sunset beaches · to reach Koh Lipe you take a boat from Pak Bara Pier (Satun) or a pier in a nearby province, then a longtail to the beach · the hostel has a desk to help book ferry tickets and tours.

faq.q: What are Bloom Hostel's starting rates and room types?
faq.a: Dorm beds start from around ฿320/bed for the 8-bed mixed dorm · the 4-bed female-only dorm is about ฿390 · the 6-bed dorm about ฿350 · the Private Double Room (shared bathroom) about ฿1,100 · every dorm bed has a privacy curtain, power outlet and locker · rates swing by season and climb at peak, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Bloom Cafe & Hostel best for?
faq.a: Best for solo travellers, budget-minded couples or backpackers who want a clean, central place to sleep and save their money for diving · it's strong on cleanliness, curtained beds and good coffee · if you want a beachfront room or total silence, a beachfront stay will suit you better.

faq.q: What are Bloom's dorms like, is there any privacy?
faq.a: Dorm beds are bunk beds that use stairs instead of ladders, and every bed has a privacy curtain, a power outlet and a locker · reviews say it sleeps private, almost like a capsule · there's a female-only dorm for those who want it · for full privacy, you can book the Private Double Room.

faq.q: What is Bloom's cafe like, and is breakfast included?
faq.a: The downstairs cafe does specialty coffee, smoothie bowls and fresh-ingredient breakfasts that reviews single out · breakfast isn't included in the room rate — you order it at the cafe — though free coffee and tea are in the common area · it's a relaxed spot to work or plan tours.

faq.q: Is Bloom Hostel noisy, and when should you visit?
faq.a: The hostel is next to Maya Bar and on the central lane, so on late bar nights you may hear music, especially in the front rooms — ask for an inner room or pack earplugs · the best time is Nov–Apr with calm, clear seas · the rainy season (May–Oct) brings strong monsoon, many island places close and ferries run less, so always check before booking.
